summary:
We developed **MechaClaw**, an affordable, 2-in-1 motorized mechanical grabber and jar opener designed using Tinkercad, an Arduino-compatible microcontroller, an L293D motor driver, and a geared DC motor. Featuring an extendable shaft, intuitive handle controls, and a rubber-lined aluminum/steel claw, the device helps users easily grip tight lids and retrieve hard-to-reach objects from high shelves, behind furniture, or off the floor.

MechaClaw addresses the NASA space-hardware challenge by using a familiar, everyday prototype to introduce school-age students to the core robotics behind off-world exploration. Just as MechaClaw extends human reach and grip strength on Earth, NASA's robotic arms and samplers—from Apollo lunar tools to Mars rovers like Perseverance—rely on remote actuation and precision gripping to collect samples and conduct science in environments humans cannot safely reach.

This project is important because it achieves dual impact: it improves daily independence and comfort for seniors and everyday households at a low cost of RM 70–RM 80, while simultaneously turning real-world engineering into an accessible, hands-on lesson that inspires young learners to understand how NASA hardware unlocks discoveries across our solar system.
details:
MechaClaw is a multi-purpose mechanical grabbing and twisting tool designed to extend a user's reach and provide extra grip leverage for everyday objects, functioning both as a high-reach/rubbish grabber and a jar or bottle cap opener. It operates through an electronic actuation system where a microcontroller and an L293D motor driver IC control a geared DC motor, opening and closing a rubber-padded claw mounted on an extendable shaft via power and directional buttons on the handle. This design offers significant benefits by promoting accessibility and independence for the elderly or those with limited grip strength, while saving everyday effort when retrieving items from high shelves, behind wardrobes, or off the floor—all at an affordable build cost of around RM 70–RM 80. Beyond improving daily household lifestyles, the project's intended impact is to serve as an educational bridge to space robotics, demonstrating how basic remote actuation and precision gripping mirror the robotic arms NASA uses on lunar landers and Mars rovers to safely gather samples in unreachable environments.

To develop MechaClaw, the team used Tinkercad to create the 3D prototype model alongside a combination of mechanical and electronic hardware. The physical build pairs a reinforced plastic or metal frame and mounting brackets with a high-strength steel or aluminum alloy claw lined with rubber straps, driven by a geared DC motor. On the electronics side, the system relies on a microcontroller (such as an Arduino, Raspberry Pi, or Intel Galileo Gen1 Board programmed with standard microcontroller logic like C/C++ or Python), an L293D IC driver, male-to-male and male-to-female jumper wires, and a rechargeable 7.2V Ni-MH battery pack. The creativity of the project lies in its 2-in-1 hybrid concept that merges two distinct household tools into a single motorized, ergonomic device with intuitive tactile controls. Throughout development, the team carefully considered cost-effectiveness to keep the device within a tight budget, balanced material strength against lightweight handling, and tailored the handle ergonomics to solve real-world physical challenges faced by everyday users and seniors.
